"Outside Taiwan medial and final *n and *N have merged in all languages" (p. 582); compare the PMP forms of Table 8.28 (aNak > anak, CaNem > tanem, daNum > danum, pp. 584-585).

"In initial position *N may have merged with *l rather than *n", since otherwise doublets in l- and n- must be accepted (*laŋuy/naŋuy, *lesuŋ/nesuŋ, *luka/nuka) (p. 582); there is no clear evidence for *N- (p. 583).
Assignment of *g to both PMP and PAN is well supported (p. 564); PAN *gaCel, *gemgem etc. and PMP *gagar, *pager (pp. 579-581).

Stated against POC *p: *pakiwak > pahko "shark", *pan(ou)(n) > pahngon "to call" (p. 405); the factor conditioning the retention of *p "is evidently not the presence of a following *a" and is not evident (p. 406).
Stated against POC *p: *patu > yot "stone", perhaps from a palatalised *p; "a single instance ... is not much basis for any kind of generalisation" (p. 405).
Stated against POC *t, "most frequently reflected as KSR t" (p. 406): *tama, *tani(s), *tolu, *tuʔu, *pitu, *natu, *ʔutup, *muta(ʔ), *matolu.

Stated against POC *t followed by *i or *e (p. 406): *tia(n) > (in-)siyac- "belly"; in *ŋkinit > kihnis and *mpulut > fulus the *i is a transitive suffix *-i (Harrison 1978), later lost (pp. 406, 430-431).
Stated against POC *t followed by *i or *e (p. 406): *ʔate > acsyac-/esyac- "liver".
Stated against POC *t: *tali > suc "rope", in an environment where t would be expected (p. 406).
Stated against POC *t: *tina > ninac "mother", "an idiosyncratic change in the initial segment" (p. 406), "most plausibly explained as a sporadic change" (p. 436, n. 5).
Stated against POC *k, reflected as k in non-final position (p. 406): *kianto, *kinta, *tuki, *kuRita, *kali, *nsakaRu, *waka.
Stated against POC *ŋk (POc *g), which "appears to have merged ... with *k", on two forms (p. 408): *mpeŋka > fak, *ŋkinit > kihnis. POc *g became PMc *x (Bender et al. 2003a: 4).

Stated against POC *mp (POc *b): *mpaya > pa "bait", the one exception to *mp > f; the source also considers *pani as the etymon, or a rule *mp > p before *a (p. 407). POc *mp not before a round vowel became PMc *p (Bender et al. 2003a: 4).

Stated against POC *mp (POc *b), which "appears to become KSR f" (p. 407): *mpo-, *mponot, *mpou, *mpoŋi, *mpule, *mpulut, *mputo, where *mp stood before a round vowel and became PMc *pʷ (Bender et al. 2003a: 4, Table 2 n. 2). Also *mpeŋka > fak "flying fox", where *mp is not before a round vowel.
Stated against POC *m, "regularly reflected as KSR m" (p. 409): *mata, *mapo, *matudu(R), *tama, *ʔuma, *lima, *tasimi.
Stated against POC *m: *manu(k) > won "bird"; no conditioning is found, and the source allows sporadic change or borrowing (p. 409).

Stated against POC *ŋm, whose "regular reflex ... might be w" (p. 410): *ŋmata > wet/wat "worm", *Ruŋma(?) > yuwac-/iwac- "house". Also POC *m in *muta(ʔ) > wihte/woht "to vomit", which the source leaves unexplained (p. 409); POc *m before a round vowel became PMc *mʷ (Bender et al. 2003a: 4, Table 2 n. 2).

Stated against POC *ŋm: *Ruŋma(?) > lohm "house", beside the regular yuwac-/iwac-; both its initial l and final m are irregular, and it may be a borrowing ("indirect inheritance", Biggs 1965), though no donor is known (p. 410).
Stated against POC *m: *-mu > -m, 2sg possessive suffix (p. 409). POc *m before a round vowel became PMc *mʷ (Bender et al. 2003a: 4).
Stated against POC *n, "normally reflected as KSR n" in non-final position (p. 409): *manipi(s), *niu(R), *ŋkinit, *manu(k), *panua, *natu, *inu(m).
Stated against POC *ŋ, which in non-final position "normally remains" ŋ (p. 409): *laŋi(t), *ŋapulu(ʔ), *ʔuluŋa, *paŋ(ou)(n), *doŋo, *mpoŋi.
Stated against POC *l, normally l in non-final position (p. 410): *sulu, *walu, *tolu, *lima, *lano, *sili.
Stated against POC *d in the orthography of Grace (1969) (POc *r): "KSR l appears to be also the regular reflex of *d" (p. 410): *daʔa(n), *doŋo, *dua, *madama, *matudu(R), *maʔudi(p), *tudu(ʔ).

Stated against POC *(dr), Grace's writing of a segment with evidence for both *d and *r (p. 435, n. 11), which "seems to be regularly reflected as r" (p. 411): *pi(dr)i > ir "twist", *si(dr)i(t) > iri. The source suggests that KSR points to *r rather than *d in these forms and notes the shared environment *i_*i, which "may or may not be relevant"; words with r are often onomatopoeic or loans (p. 411). Bender et al. (2003a: 5, Table 3 n. 6) take KSR r as diagnostic of loans.

Stated against POC *nd (POc *dr), "regularly reflected in KSR as the retroflexed fricative sr" (p. 411): *ndanu(m) > sroano-, *ndau(n) > sra; and against POC *nt (POc *d) in *punti > usr (p. 408). POc *d and *dr became PMc *c (Bender et al. 2003a: 5).
Stated against POC *nt (POc *d): *kinta > kuht "we"; with three instances of *nt "it is difficult to arrive at any conclusions regarding the regular development" (p. 408).
Stated against POC *nt (POc *d): *kianto > kiyacs "outrigger boom", for which there is an alternative reconstruction with *t, and "KSR s suggests *t" (p. 408).

Stated against POC *s, which "appears to have been lost in forms in which it preceded *i" (p. 408): *ʔanusi > acni, *si(dr)i(t) > iri, *sili > il, *tasimi > twem; ordered before *t > s and final vowel deletion (pp. 430-431). Bender et al. (2003a: 5) give KSR s for PMc *s before *i and *e.
Stated against POC *s, "sometimes preserved as KSR s" (p. 408): *sulu > sul, *sae(t) > se.
Stated against POC *s: *susu > titi- "breast", where *s became t "under conditions which would appear to favour preservation of s" (p. 408).

Stated against POC *ns, which "it appears to be the rule" is lost (p. 408): *nsake > -yak/-ack, *nsani > eng, *nsiwa > yuh, *tansi(k) > te. POC *ns became PMc *S (Bender et al. 2003a: 5, Table 3 n. 1).
Stated against POC *ns: *nsai > suc "who?"; the two non-zero reflexes differ "in what appears to be the same environment" (p. 408).
Stated against POC *ns: *nsakaRu > tuhka "island"; the two non-zero reflexes differ "in what appears to be the same environment" (p. 408).
Stated against POC *y: *mpaya > pa "bait", the only instance; "It is not clear that *y was phonemic in POC" (p. 412).

Stated against POC *w, "generally ... lost in KSR, although not always without leaving some trace of its presence on the vowels" (p. 412): *waka > okah (where *wa "appears to have coalesced as o"), *nsiwa > yuh, *pakiwak > pahko, *waRo > ah, *walu > oal-. The summary table also lists w (p. 405).
